purpose: Azilsartan medoxomil is used to treat high blood pressure, also called hypertension. Keeping your blood pressure under control helps lower your risk of having a heart attack or stroke. Your doctor may prescribe it alone or along with other blood pressure medicines.
how_it_works: Your body makes a natural chemical called angiotensin II that tightens and narrows your blood vessels, which raises your blood pressure. This medicine blocks the receptors that angiotensin II attaches to, so your blood vessels can relax and widen. When your blood vessels are more relaxed, your heart does not have to work as hard, and your blood pressure goes down.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is dizziness, especially when you stand up quickly. You may also notice tiredness, diarrhea, or nausea. These effects are usually mild and often improve as your body adjusts to the medicine.
warnings: Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can seriously harm an unborn baby. Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, or if you are taking water pills (diuretics), as your blood pressure may drop too low. Avoid potassium supplements or salt substitutes containing potassium unless your doctor approves, since this drug can raise potassium levels in your blood.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 80 mg taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. Some people start at 40 mg once a day if they are also taking a high-dose diuretic. Try to take it at the same time each day, and never stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
